comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore empty directories that init records independently**

After `rh init --mode minimal` in a fresh Git repository, `rh config restore --repo` leaves `.ai/harness/checks` behind even though init created and recorded it. This filter includes a directory only when a reverted file lies inside it, so directories that init creates empty never qualify. `revertWholePaths` uses the same restriction. I reproduced this with the reviewed runtime: restore removed the file records but retained the empty directory and its ledger entry; subsequent restore attempts cannot clean it because there are no path records left. Include independently recorded empty directories in both the restore plan and its apply.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**P1 init-retirement-discards-staged-user-bytes**

The retirement proof checks working-tree bytes. Git untrack force-removes the index entry even when it contains a different staged-only blob, a state exercised in tests/cli/adoption-plan.test.ts:988. The new success path keeps no durable record of that blob or its mode, while the converted test restores the exact stage only after an injected failure. The sole undo command has no index record.

**Fix**: Before removing the file or index entry, refuse retirement if the index contains staged-only user content, or durably preserve the blob and mode and restore them through rh config restore --repo. Cover the successful-run case with a regression.

Fixed in a7acf6c24. Before any remove or untrack, the run checks each retirement: the index entry must hold exactly the proved working-tree bytes (`git hash-object --no-filters` equals the index object id). Otherwise the remove and the untrack are skipped with a `kept` reason; the file and the index entry stay, the run succeeds, and `rh init` prints `[init] kept: <path> - …`. The dry run uses the same check. Regression: `a successful run keeps a retired helper and its index entry when the index holds a staged user edit` (fails without the fix). The in-run rollback case now stages the canonical bytes, since a staged edit is no longer untracked.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include closed, unreleased trains in release-set selection**

When a migration or ledger train finishes, this new condition prevents its selection until the batch parent closes. However, steps 1–2 build the candidate trains from open issues only, and `orchestrator.md` §10 requires all children to be closed or shelved before parent closeout. Completed trains therefore disappear from the candidate list before they become eligible. Include closed, unreleased trains in the selection procedure so these changes can enter the release milestone and receive release tracking.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed in 1694d4d45: the rule now gates release timing, not train selection; merged work ships with the first release after the parent closes, and a fix release for a released I1/I2 defect stays allowed. Seat: orchestrator t2mn
